title: Lagged real disposable-income year-over-year growth acceleration for BTC long or cash
thesis: A conservatively lagged monthly acceleration in U.S. real disposable personal-income year-over-year growth may identify improving household risk-bearing capacity with better subsequent Bitcoin risk-adjusted economics than nonaccelerating months.
mechanism: Using only the sealed present-vintage DSPIC96 monthly series, compute DSPIC96_t divided by DSPIC96_t-minus-12 minus one and subtract the immediately prior month's analogous year-over-year rate. Make the state usable on the first day of the second following month at 00:00 UTC. Hold full-capital unlevered BTC only when the adjacent year-over-year growth change is strictly positive, and zero-yield cash otherwise. No transfers, savings, consumption, payrolls, absolute-growth level, magnitude threshold, smoothing, alternate lag, inverse direction or combined factor is allowed.
economic_rationale: If accelerating inflation-adjusted after-tax household resources improve risk-bearing capacity, the policy may avoid nonaccelerating drawdowns while retaining enough BTC upside to improve matched-capital Calmar after explicit normal and doubled friction. Because fiscal transfers and saving can break the mechanism, Design, Validation, annual breadth, episode concentration and terminal inventory must all pass.
